newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Megawati harshly criticises government.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Megawati harshly criticises government.

text.p: Indonesia's best-known opposition figure has said the country is in decline because of a lack of democracy, widespread corruption and a flawed legal system.

Megawati Sukarnoputri said in an article received by Reuters on Monday that the restoration of democracy in Indonesia was the top agenda item "in our effort to bring about improvements in our political, economic, social and bureaucratic life".
Copies of the article were distributed to the diplomatic corps in Jakarta, said aides of Megawati, who was ousted last year as head of the minority Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI).

"This kind of situation cannot be left unimproved," she wrote. "If we want to maintain our existence as a nation with genuine political and economic sovereignty...then we have to do something to restore all kinds of distortions that have plagued us during these last five years."

Megawati, daughter of late founding president Sukarno, did not name President Suharto or any member of his government in the 20-page article. But it is the first time she has publicly launched a detailed criticism of his policies.

"We have to stop nepotism in our public life. We have to restore the independence of the judicial system, making it impossible for any part of the executive system to interfere with the processes of justice," she said.

"We have to do our best to reduce and finally wipe out corruption, collusion and abuse of power. We have to strive towards clean and competent governments, both at the national and local levels," Megawati said.

She noted that in theory, the 1,000-member People's Consultative Assembly (MPR), which consists of 500 members of parliament and 500 nominated members, was the most powerful institution in the country.

"In practice, however, it is the president who wields the highest power in the state. Members of the MPR, outside members (of parliament), are selected by a committee which works under the close scrutiny of the president.
"No one can become a member of the MPR without the personal approval of the incumbent president," she said, adding that all its members should be freely elected.
She said the government controlled the media and exercised an unhealthy influence over the legal system.

"It has become a forum where exective power looms behind every legal skirmish and intimidates those lawyers whose position in the disputed case happens to be different from that held by the executive."
Megawati said members of the executive "exerted influence on judges" and that "our courts are still considered corrupt by the public".
Indonesia holds parliamentary elections next month, but Megawati is not on the list of approved candidates.
The government allows only members of three parties -- the ruling Golkar, the PDI and the Moslem-oriented United Development Party -- to contest elections.
Following her ouster from the PDI by a government-backed faction, neither Megawati nor her supporters have been among the candidates put forward by her party.
